limits: The new ideal experiment independently samples a width-bit raw value and reduces it modulo the group order. Its bound is DDH advantage plus five sampling errors; the old exact-uniform ideal challenge keeps its four-error result.
The original width lower bound proves the five-error term negligible; this replay does not prove the same finite bound 2^-n for that term.
Sampler and complete-game resource results count at most the stated number of fair-coin queries, not deterministic work or honest group-operation runtime.

The security theorem retains explicit primitive contracts, DDH hardness, backend composition and concrete encoding certificates. No conventional machine adequacy or native implementation family is instantiated.
The parameter-polynomial randomness theorem additionally assumes polynomial input-size and sampling-width upper bounds. It does not certify canonical unary parameter encoding.
Historical extraction, native tests, concrete endpoints and prior replay records remain unchanged.
